claims.original_statement: Whether a comparison K to its truncation homotopy limit is an isomorphism is independent of the lift; the split injective tower is a resolution exactly when that comparison is an isomorphism.
claims.proved_statement: For A_p=H^p(P), delta_p=H^p(Delta), and the stable projection q_p:ker delta_p to H^p(K), the recovery defect E_p has exact sequence 0 to coker delta_(p-1) to E_p to ker q_p to 0. Every chosen comparison gives the explicit decomposition H^p(C)=H^p(K) direct-sum E_p. It is an isomorphism exactly when both stated defect terms vanish in every degree.
claims.hypotheses: An abelian category and existence in D(A) of the product of the actual canonical truncation tower and its homotopy limit; no exactness of products or enough-injectives assumption.
claims.limits: The defect and projection maps are independent of the comparison lift, but the direct-sum identification uses that chosen lift. No general vanishing is assumed.

claims.original_statement: Under enough injectives and exact countable products, the proof establishes truncation recovery and then a K-injective resolution.
claims.proved_statement: Exact countable products alone give truncation recovery. More generally the actual cohomology of a tower homotopy limit has the kernel-cokernel exact sequence of its cohomology difference maps; eventual cohomology isomorphisms in each degree give convergence, with a degree-dependent stabilization index. All transition factors and the splitting of the difference map are explicit.
claims.hypotheses: Exact countable products in the abelian category. Enough injectives are retained when concluding the source K-injective resolution construction.
claims.limits: No removal of the source enough-injectives hypothesis from its K-injective existence conclusion; no substitution of product exactness for exactness of all inverse limits.
